newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean inflation at a mere 0.2 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Chilean inflation at a mere 0.2 pct in May.

text.p: Consumer prices rose 0.2 percent in Chile last month, compared with 0.8 percent in May last year and the smallest monthly increase in recent memory, the National Statistics Institute reported.
The figure brought inflation in the first five months of the year to 2.2 percent and 5.4 percent over the last 12 months, said the institute.
The government's inflation target for the whole calendar year is 5.8 percent while the Central Bank's target is 5.5 to six percent.
Prices on exportable goods were unchanged in May, while non-exportable goods showed a rise of 0.4 percent, it said.

By category, food prices were unchanged in May as were transport and communications prices. Housing prices rose 0.8 percent and apparel prices fell 0.4 percent, while the catch-all "other" category showed a 0.2 percent rise, said the institute.
By comparison, consumer inflation in the 12 months through May 1996 was 8.6 percent.
